admission.justification: The recorded behavioral fixture assertions guard this obligation; the proof facets distinguish their limited fixture behavior from real-host or full-final acceptance.

applicability: Every serving sweep tick over a recipient's held store, and the turn-end drain that runs beside it.
conditions: The tick runs under the serving loop's ledger accounting; the queue holds the receipts that carry waiting messages.
The sweep's own per-tick read and drain budgets stay at thirty-two.
The turn-end drain is driven by the host's activity record for the agents whose turn just ended and is not part of that thirty-two-read sweep budget.
exclusions: The queue is not a census of all receipt paths; a directory listing is materialised once per pass.
History and message-binding subtrees are never descended into.

evidence: mcp/tests/test_held_queue.py::HeldSweepBoundsTests::test_idle_fleet_reads_stay_bounded_at_two_sizes passes with zero rglob yields; scratch/worker/5e0b3a10-7a35-4c5e-9f11-100000000001/xdg/r6-probe-after.txt sha 628ed08eb73c: 0 enumerated paths all six cycles at 64/256, reads<=32 (rglob API; per-directory scandir listings materialize once per pass, disclosed residual for Architect inspection)

statement: Each sweep tick drains the receipts whose turn just ended, then the queued held receipts through a rotating slice, and only then walks at most thirty-two candidate receipt paths and reads at most thirty-two receipts; no recursive glob runs in the tick, history and bindings are never descended into, and the rotation reaches every queued receipt within a bounded number of ticks.
